title: A meta-analysis on the effects of service-learning on the social, personal, and cognitive outcomes of learning
authors: Patrick L. Yorio; Feifei Ye
synthesis: Quantifies social, personal, and cognitive effects across service-learning studies.
finding: Service-learning was positively associated with all three outcome families; structured reflection was among the design features examined.
limitations: Primary studies were heterogeneous and business-education evidence was limited.

title: Experiential learning in entrepreneurship education: A systematic literature review
authors: Victória Figueiredo Motta; Simone Vasconcelos Ribeiro Galina
synthesis: Synthesizes experiential-learning approaches in entrepreneurship education.
finding: Experiential formats generally aligned with stronger entrepreneurial intentions and skills, while designs and measures varied substantially.
limitations: Domain-specific review; heterogeneous interventions prevent a single causal estimate.

title: A meta-analysis of the impact of service-learning on students
authors: Christine I. Celio; Joseph Durlak; Allison Dymnicki
synthesis: Estimates student effects and examines program-design moderators.
finding: Effects ranged roughly from .27 to .43; curriculum links, student voice, community involvement, and reflection were associated with better outcomes.
limitations: Nonrandom primary studies and heterogeneity limit causal interpretation.

title: Service learning in higher education: A systematic literature review
authors: Maimoona Salam; Dayang Nurfatimah Awang Iskandar; Dayang Hanani Abang Ibrahim; Muhammad Shoaib Farooq
synthesis: Maps higher-education service-learning research, outcomes, and implementation themes.
finding: The field reports academic, personal, social, and civic outcomes across diverse settings.
limitations: Quality appraisal is less explicit than the breadth of mapping; findings are not one pooled effect.

title: Implementing service learning in higher education
authors: Robert G. Bringle; Julie A. Hatcher
synthesis: Introduces an institutional framework for implementing service-learning in higher education.
finding: Positions coordinated institutional structures, faculty support, curriculum, students, and community as linked implementation components.
limitations: Conceptual and metadata/abstract-only in this audit; not an outcome test.

title: Institutionalization of service learning in higher education
authors: Robert G. Bringle; Julie A. Hatcher
synthesis: Examines institutionalization using the CAPSL framework.
finding: Shows that durable service-learning requires alignment across institutional constituencies rather than isolated courses.
limitations: Preliminary, self-reported institutional evidence.

title: A theoretical and practical framework for service-learning in marketing: Kolb’s experiential learning cycle
authors: Ed Petkus
synthesis: Applies Kolb's experiential-learning cycle to marketing service-learning.
finding: Connects concrete experience, reflection, conceptualization, and experimentation to course design.
limitations: One disciplinary case; no controlled outcome test.

title: Theoretical underpinnings of service learning
authors: Rebecca Lynn Carver
synthesis: Explains why service-learning effects vary through belonging, competence, and change-agent mechanisms.
finding: Benefits depend on how experience is structured and interpreted, not on service activity alone.
limitations: Theoretical propositions require empirical testing.

title: Sustainable development through service learning: A pedagogical framework and case example in a third world context
authors: Holly H. Brower
synthesis: Links service-learning, social enterprise, and sustainable community development.
finding: A short case illustrates a framework for integrating community problems into management learning.
limitations: Two faculty and eight students over one month; dated contextual language and no controlled outcomes.

title: Organizing reflection to address collective dilemmas: Engaging students and professors with sustainable development in higher education
authors: Janette Brunstein; Jeff King
synthesis: Studies organized reflection as a response to collective sustainability dilemmas.
finding: Institutionalized reflection linked student projects, faculty practice, and transformative-learning goals.
limitations: Single-university case; mechanisms are contextual rather than causal.

title: How students’ motivation and learning experience affect their service- learning outcomes: A structural equation modeling analysis
authors: Kenneth W. K. Lo; Grace Ngai; Stephen C. F. Chan; Kam-por Kwan
study_design: Structural equation modeling; more than 2,000 students in 132 courses
synthesis: Tests links among motivation, learning experience, and service-learning outcomes.
finding: Motivation and learning experience were associated with cognitive learning and other outcomes.
limitations: Observational SEM does not establish causal direction; Hong Kong context.

title: Integrating service-learning into an introduction to entrepreneurship course
authors: Elizabeth A. McCrea
synthesis: Integrates service-learning into an introductory entrepreneurship course.
finding: The model emphasizes ambiguity management, entrepreneurial skills, and self-efficacy through authentic community work.
limitations: Primarily instructor reflection without a controlled comparison.

title: Beyond the classroom: Integrating the ORID model for in-depth reflection and assessment in service-learning
authors: FK Fadlelmula; SM Qadhi
synthesis: Uses the ORID model for structured reflection and assessment.
finding: ORID prompts surfaced objective, reflective, interpretive, and decisional dimensions of student learning.
limitations: Single-event context and no comparison group.

title: The development of high leverage practices in environmental sustainability-focused service learning courses: applications for higher education
authors: Byung-Yeol Park; Rebecca Campbell-Montalvo; Todd Campbell; Hannah Cooke; Chester Arnold; John C. Volin; Maria Chrysochoou; Peter C. Diplock
synthesis: Identifies high-leverage practices in sustainability-focused service-learning.
finding: An epistemic community iteratively developed practices connecting environmental problems, partners, and student work.
limitations: Course-development evidence rather than a causal outcome evaluation.

title: Does service-learning add value? Examining the perspectives of multiple stakeholders
authors: Scott W. Lester; Chuck Tomkovick; Theresa Wells; Lanette Flunker; Jill Kickul
synthesis: Compares value perceptions among students, recruiters, and project supervisors.
finding: All stakeholder groups perceived value, but valued different outcomes, supporting multi-party design and assessment.
limitations: Cross-sectional perceptions and one mandated 30-hour setting.

title: Whom does service learning really serve? Community-based organizations' perspectives on service learning
authors: David D. Blouin; Evelyn M. Perry
synthesis: Centers organizational partners rather than treating them as passive beneficiaries.
finding: Partners reported benefits and costs involving student conduct, fit, capacity, and coordination; net value was conditional.
limitations: Interview evidence is contextual and does not estimate comparative effects.

title: Co-constructing knowledge in uganda: Host community conceptions of relationships in international service-learning
authors: Kari Grain; Tonny Katumba; Dennis Kirumira; Rosemary Nakasiita; Saudah Nakayenga; Eseza Nankya; Vicent Nteza; Micheal Ssegawa
study_design: Photovoice and qualitative co-construction in Uganda
synthesis: Examines host-community conceptions of relationships in international service-learning.
finding: Participants emphasized friendship, education, social change, and persistent power tensions.
limitations: Specific international context and interpretive methods limit transferability.

title: Critical service-learning supports social justice and civic engagement orientations in college students
authors: Jean Abigail Saavedra; Lizette Ruiz; Lucía Alcalá
journal: Michigan Journal of Community Service Learning
study_design: Mixed methods; 125 students in three psychology classes
synthesis: Tests critical service-learning's relationship to social-justice and civic orientations.
finding: Participants showed stronger justice and civic orientations alongside qualitative evidence of perspective change.
limitations: Nonrandom course comparison limits causal claims.

title: Community partners' experiences of higher education service-learning in a community engagement module
authors: Martina Jordaan; Nita Mennega
journal: Journal of Applied Research in Higher Education
synthesis: Examines partners as co-educators in a community-engagement module.
finding: Reciprocity depended on communication, role clarity, and recognizing community expertise.
limitations: Abstract/metadata-only in this audit; one institutional context.

title: The impact of mandatory academic service-learning on university graduates’ continual civic engagement: evidence from a curriculum reform
authors: Shuheng Lin; Grace Ngai; Kam Por Kwan; Stephen C.F. Chan; Kenneth W.K. Lo
study_design: Curriculum-reform cohort comparison with regression controls
synthesis: Examines long-term civic engagement after mandatory academic service-learning.
finding: Graduates exposed to the reform were estimated to be 9.4% more likely to remain civically engaged, with larger effects among those without prior service.
limitations: Quasi-experimental rather than randomized; civic outcome and institutional context constrain inference.

title: ‘I can succeed at this’: Engagement in service learning in schools enh ances university students’ self-efficacy
authors: Raphael Gutzweiler; Simone Pfeiffer; Tina In-Albon
synthesis: Tracks general and teaching self-efficacy across two years of school service-learning.
finding: Pre-post gains were reported for general self-efficacy (d=.30) and teaching self-efficacy (d=.68), with feedback-related patterns.
limitations: No randomized control; repeated measures do not isolate service-learning from co-occurring influences.

title: Student learning through service learning: Effects on academic development, civic responsibility, interpersonal skills and practical skills
authors: Ali Hébert; Petra Hauf
study_design: Course comparison: 23 service-learning and 107 comparison students
synthesis: Compares academic, civic, interpersonal, and practical outcomes.
finding: No final-exam advantage appeared, but course-specific civic, interpersonal, and practical benefits were reported.
limitations: Small treatment group and nonrandom enrollment.

title: Service-Learning in Higher Education and Prosocial Identity Formation
authors: Lindsey M. McDougle; Huafang Li
synthesis: Links service-learning to prosocial role-identity formation.
finding: Offers a structural-symbolic-interactionist model for how repeated roles and recognition may stabilize prosocial identity.
limitations: Conceptual model, not an empirical test.

title: Impactful social entrepreneurship education: A US-spanish service learning collaborative online international learning (COIL) project
authors: Maria Ballesteros-Sola; Nina Magomedova
journal: The International Journal of Management Education
synthesis: Studies a seven-week US-Spain service-learning COIL project with social enterprises.
finding: Students reported personal, social, and cognitive competency development through cross-border team problem solving.
limitations: Researcher-participant bias, exploratory design, and no strong comparison.

title: Skills and knowledge management in higher education: How service learning can contribute to social entrepreneurial competence development
authors: Jantje Halberstadt; Jana-Michaela Timm; Sascha Kraus; Katherine Gundolf
study_design: Mixed qualitative content analysis; 40 master's students and five instructors
synthesis: Develops a social-entrepreneurial competence framework from service-learning diaries and interviews.
finding: Identifies knowledge, skills, and reflective processes connecting service-learning to social entrepreneurial competence.
limitations: Small German sample; framework needs longitudinal and comparative validation.
